newsitem.title: USA: Key senator slams U.S. EPA 1998 budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Key senator slams U.S. EPA 1998 budget plan.

text.p: Sen. Christopher Bond, a Missouri Republican, Tuesday criticised the Environmental Protection Agency's budget plan for the 1998 fiscal year, especially a 50 percent hike in money for toxic waste cleanups.
EPA asked Congress for $7.6 billion for the next fiscal year which begins in October, up more than 10 percent from this year.
"Not surprisingly, I don't believe EPA's proposal is realistic in the current budget environment," said Bond, chairman of the Senate subcommittee in charge of allocating funds for EPA.

Most of the increase in the budget request was due to a proposed $650 million increase in spending on Superfund toxic waste cleanups to live up to a campaign promise by President Clinton, EPA Administrator Carol Browner said.
"Until (Superfund) legislative reform is adopted, I cannot support any increase in this programme," Bond said at a hearing on the agency's budget proposal.
Bond and the top Democrat on the subcommittee, Sen. Barbara Mikulski of Maryland, both raised concern about a proposed cut of $275 million in funding to states for clean water projects.
"If additional funds are found within our (subcommittee) allocation, my highest priority within EPA will be restoring the cut to the clean water state revolving fund," Bond said.

Despite the criticism, in contrast to two years when Republicans wanted to slash EPA's budget to cut enforcement and issuing of environmental regulations, Bond said EPA's 1998 spending would likely be frozen at this year's level.
